title: itembank course operation request
description: The published request document for POST /api/course/<operation> and its CLI twin. One $defs node per operation, and the node IS the operation's signature: the Phase 999.3 MCP tool table generates one tool per API_ROUTES entry and reads its argument shape from here, so a schema edit changes the tool with no code edit. The top-level oneOf makes the whole file a single valid contract a reader can validate a captured request against; dispatch validates against the one named node the route's own path selects, so a refusal names the field rather than reporting that no branch matched. This document describes a REQUEST and never a durable object: course_graph.schema.json is the sidecar the operations write, write_manifest.schema.json is the writer's provenance record, and neither is reshaped to carry a request. No request field names a filesystem path, a fingerprint of another object, a right the caller claims to hold, or a score: a course is addressed by its id and resolved server-side, and every right a write consumes is read from the operation journal at the moment of that write. The one node that names rights is `rights`, and it records a decision rather than asserting a permission.

course_id.description: The course's opaque identity, as the shelf and the /course/<course_id> route already spell it: either the pinned course_object_id or, for a course being created, the directory name it is minted under. The pattern is the route's own, so no request can carry a path separator, a parent reference, or a name a URL could not hold.

title.description: The course's human-readable title, written into the sidecar header. Titles are display, never identity: renaming a course never changes its course_object_id and never touches its evidence.

actor.description: Who is recording this, as it appears in the operation journal. Optional and free text; the actor kind is decided by the surface, never by the request.

expected_fingerprint.description: The fingerprint the caller believes the sidecar currently carries. Passed straight to journal.commit_operation, which refuses a stale write by name with journal.stale_preflight. Omitted means the operation reads the current fingerprint itself, which is a last-writer-wins convenience for a single-surface caller and not a substitute for compare-and-swap when two clients can write.

source_object_id.description: The opaque id of a source object this course root's journal registry already holds, as `itembank bind list` prints it. Opaque on purpose and matched by no pattern here: an id is minted by identity.py and a request that guessed at its shape would be asserting something only the registry knows.

objective_id.description: The id of an objective already recorded in this course's sidecar. Unrecognised ids are refused by graph.add_binding, not here, so the refusal can say which endpoints the course actually holds.

locator.description: Where in the source the claim points: a path, an anchor, a page, a timestamp. A coverage claim points and reproduces nothing, which is why binding a source consumes `read` and never `quote`.

treatment_kind.description: Which of the eleven treatments this is, TREAT-01's closed vocabulary as `graph.TREATMENT_KINDS` spells it. The vocabulary is published ONCE, here, and every node that names a treatment refs this one: the enum is a copy of an engine tuple, a copy drifts, and two copies drift apart twice as fast. tests/course_ops_roundtrip.py asserts this list equals that tuple and asserts that no other node inlines its own, because a published document that names a treatment the engine does not have, or omits one it does, refuses a legitimate binding on every surface at once. Which right a treatment consumes is NOT published here and is not a request field: it is `graph.TREATMENT_RIGHTS`, read by the runtime at the moment of the write and reported by the `treatments` operation.

binding_state.description: How well this binding claims the objective is covered. `unknown` is the default at every surface and `covered` is never a default: coverage is a claim someone makes, not a side effect of recording a row.

confidence.description: How sure the claim is. Defaults to `unknown`.

grants.description: The rights decision being recorded, one closed name to one closed state. Merged onto what the object already carries, so naming one right never resets the others, and `denied` is recorded by the same operation as `granted` because a decision not to use something is as much a decision as its opposite. A right absent from this object is left as it was, and a right that was never recorded reads as `unknown`, which refuses.

statement.description: What the learner will be able to do, in one sentence. An objective statement is authored text and never inferred from a heading.

rationale.description: Why this change to objective identity is proposed, in the author's words. Required rather than optional: GRAPH-04 makes every identity move a reviewed proposal, and a proposal a reviewer cannot read the reason for is not reviewable.

order.description: The authored position of this row within its section. Omitted means the end. Authored order is primary and nothing reorders it silently, so this is the one place a position is decided.

edge_type.description: Which of D-14A-1's four frozen relations this edge asserts. A type outside this list is not accepted from a surface, though a row already carrying one is kept and read as `recommended-before`, because a relation a human wrote down is evidence about the course even when this build cannot act on it.

edge_authority.description: Where the claim comes from. Defaults to `proposed`, the least-blocking value, so a surface that says nothing claims nothing.

edge_override.description: How hard this edge blocks. `hard-gate` is the exceptional value GRAPH-02 names: it is never a default, a human has to write it explicitly, and no degraded reading can reach it. Blocking a learner is not something a typo may do.

create.description: Mint a course: one course-graph.md sidecar written through journal.commit_operation as a mint, with every section empty. Reaches course.create_course and writes nothing else.

rename.description: Retitle an existing course: one edit_in_place through course.write_course, changing the sidecar header's title and nothing else. Identity, objectives, sources, bindings and evidence are untouched.

add_source.description: Record a reference to a source object in the course sidecar's Sources section, through graph.add_source and one compare-and-swap course.write_course. This is the step between importing a source (the journal registry holds the object) and binding it (the sidecar has to name it), and it was the one function in the source-binding family with no door at all. It copies no bytes, claims no coverage, and grants no right: rights live on the source object in the operation journal and are read fresh at every write.

title.description: A derived, regenerable annotation for a human reading the sidecar. The source file owns its own title and nothing is ever validated against this copy.

note.description: Why this source is in this course, in the author's words. Never read back for a decision.

bind.description: Bind a SOURCE to an objective as a coverage claim. Reaches course.bind_source, which refuses unless the source's `read` right is exactly granted at the moment of the write: unknown and denied both refuse, and neither is a lesser form of permission. The right consumed is never a request field; it is decided by the binding kind and read from the journal registry. DEPRECATED SECOND MODE: `binding_kind: "treatment"` with a `treatment` still records a treatment binding here, because this route served that before the spine existed and non-negotiable 4 forbids retiring it silently. It is deprecated in favour of `bind_treatment`, which requires the treatment the way this node cannot: this validator has no if/then, so `treatment` must be optional here and the requirement is enforced one call later in Python, which means the tool generated from this node advertises an optional field the runtime insists on. Both modes write the identical row through the identical gate, asserted by test; the deprecated one is retired by an explicit `migrate` once nothing calls it.

binding_kind.description: Which of the two binding kinds this is. A source binding consumes `read`; a treatment binding consumes whatever right its treatment kind consumes. `treatment` here is the deprecated second mode described above; new callers send `bind_treatment` instead.

bind_treatment.description: Bind a TREATMENT to an objective: the decision that this objective is taught by reading the source directly, or by an excerpt, a guided lesson, a worked example, a practice set, a formal test, and so on. Reaches course.bind_treatment, which looks the consumed right up through graph.treatment_right and refuses unless THAT right is exactly granted on the source at the moment of the write, so an excerpt refuses on `quote` and a guided lesson on `transform` while a direct reading needs only `read`. A right granted for one operation never implies another, and the row's rights_snapshot is history that is never read back for an authorization decision. This node exists rather than a `binding_kind` flag on `bind` because `treatment` is required here and cannot be made required there: the request document IS the generated tool signature, and a tool that advertises an optional field the runtime insists on is a tool that fails at call time instead of at type time. Ask the `treatments` operation first to see which of the eleven this source's recorded rights actually allow.

treatments.description: Read the eleven treatments, the right each one consumes, and, when a source is named, whether that right is granted on that source right now. A READ: it writes nothing and advances no revision. This is the first reader graph.TREATMENT_RIGHTS has ever had. The mapping decides which of the eleven treatments a course may use for a given source, and until this operation existed it could only be discovered by attempting a binding and being refused: a learner who had granted `read` and not `transform` could bind a direct reading and not a guided lesson, and nothing on any surface said so beforehand. Naming a source turns the static table into an answer about that source, with the count of treatment bindings this course already records for each kind beside it. It reports and never grants: the way to change an answer here is to record the right, which is the `rights` operation.

source.description: The opaque id of a source object to resolve the table against. Omitted means report the mapping and this course's recorded usage only, with every rights state left empty, which is `unknown or not asked` and never `granted`.

rights.description: Record what may be done with one source, through journal.op_grant_rights, which advances the object's revision and touches none of its bytes. This is the learner's own declaration about their own file, and it is the same act `source import --grant` performs at link time, available afterwards, because a decision about a file should not require re-importing it. It records a decision; it never asserts one on a caller's behalf, which is why no other node here accepts a rights field.

bindings.description: Read every binding this course records, with its effective reading. A READ: it writes nothing, advances no revision, and is the only operation here a cross-origin page may reach. Each row is passed through graph.validate_binding, so a state this build cannot read degrades to `unknown` and never to `covered`, and the rights the binding consumed are read FRESH through course.rights_for_binding and reported beside the snapshot recorded at bind time. A snapshot that says granted and a registry that now says denied is the one divergence a coverage claim cannot see by itself, so this operation names it.

add_container.description: Add one structural container (a module, a week, a unit) to the course sidecar through graph.add_container. It adds zero edges: a container's position in the outline is structure, not a prerequisite claim (GRAPH-01). The label is deliberately open text and matched against no list, because a course that calls its unit a fortnight is not wrong and finding out would cost a release.

label.description: What kind of container this is: program, semester, module, week, unit, chapter, or a word this course uses instead. Open vocabulary, checked against nothing.

parent.description: The id of the container this one sits inside. Omitted means top level.

add_objective.description: Add one objective through graph.add_objective. Like a container it adds zero edges. The objective is always recorded with origin `local`, and no request may claim `imported`: an imported scope binds as an immutable version under GRAPH-01, so claiming that origin from a surface would let a hand-authored row impersonate an import and become un-editable for a reason that was never true.

container.description: The id of the container this objective belongs to. Omitted means unplaced, which is a real state and not an error.

add_edge.description: Add one edge between two things this course graph already knows, through graph.add_edge. An edge has no minted id: its identity is the tuple (source, edge_type, target), so editing its rationale edits that edge rather than creating a different one. A duplicate key, a self edge, and an endpoint the graph does not hold are all refused by name rather than absorbed, because a graph that quietly swallows a contradiction is a graph nobody can trust to answer a question. Note that `source` here is an edge endpoint, which may be an objective, a container, or a source object, and is not the `source` field the bind and rights nodes carry.

source.description: The endpoint the relation runs FROM: for a prerequisite-of edge, the objective that comes first.

target.description: The endpoint the relation runs TO.

rationale.description: Why this relation holds. Optional on an edge, unlike on an identity migration, because an edge is a claim about the material and a migration is a claim about identity.

structure.description: Read the course's containers, objectives and edges, with the effective reading of each edge (graph.validate_edge) and the warnings the authored order earns (graph.validate_order). A READ: it writes nothing. It reports and never corrects, because the authored sequence is primary and a projection that silently reorders makes every future diff unreadable. Ask for `propose_order` to also get a sequence that would satisfy every prerequisite (graph.propose_order); it is returned as a proposal for a person to accept and is never written by this operation. The richer outline projection is plan 19A-09's read, not this one.

propose_order.description: Also compute an order satisfying every prerequisite edge. A prerequisite cycle is reported as a warning naming the objectives involved, never silently broken.

rename_objective.description: Restate one objective, as a reviewed proposal. A rename is a NEW row plus a migration relation and never an edit to the original: the identity the learner's evidence was recorded against stays in the file, or that evidence stops naming anything. The migration is recorded `proposed`; accepting or rejecting it is plan 19A-07's family, and until then both rows are in the sidecar and the new one carries no evidence.

split_objective.description: Split one objective into several, as a reviewed proposal. Adds rows and deletes none, for the reason rename gives. Each new identity reads `unknown` for evidence until real evidence is recorded against it: unmigrated evidence stays on the original identity, and `unknown` does not mean zero progress, it means nothing has been recorded here yet.

statements.description: The statements the objective splits into, in authored order. At least two, because a split into one is a rename and the two record different facts about identity.

merge_objectives.description: Merge several objectives into one, as a reviewed proposal. Every merged-from row stays in the file, for the reason rename gives.

objectives.description: The objectives being merged, at least two and each named once. Naming one twice would record a merge that is not one.

overlay_objective.description: Record a local revision of an IMPORTED objective as a sibling row. GRAPH-01 binds an imported scope as an immutable version, so an overlay is a new row with its own id joined to the import by an `overlays` reference and a recorded migration, and no code path targets the import's bytes at all. Nothing in an overlay chain is ever deleted; superseded rows stay in the file and stop being projected. This is the operation to reach for when a rename would be refused because the target was imported.
